title: Runtime experiment registry and reproducibility protocol
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This page defines the canonical registry, metadata contract, and execution protocol for all runtime-level experiments at Redwood Inference. It covers experiment registration, required metadata, how to capture and store traces, profiling and benchmarking steps, kernel-scheduler configuration checkpoints, runbook hooks for anomalies, and a release-note template for experiments that affect production runtime behavior.

Why this exists

Teams run many experiments that touch the serving runtime: new kernel rollouts, scheduler-policy changes, KV-cache warmup heuristics, quantization variants, and fallback routing alterations. Without a single registry and reproducible protocol we lose provenance, can’t compare results reliably, and risk unsafe rollouts. This doc is the operational contract for reproducible runtime experimentation.

Scope

- Applies to all experiments that change behavior of services under sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime (runtime-router, kernel-dispatcher, kv-cache, prefetcher, admission-controller).
- Includes lab runs, canary rollouts, and production toggle experiments.
- Excludes purely model-only experiments (those belong to applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding).

Definitions and identifiers

- Experiment ID: EXP-YYYY-NNN (e.g., EXP-2025-042). Unique across the registry.
- Artifact snapshot: git commit + container image digest (sha256).
- Kernel version: runtime kernel semantic tag (e.g., k-2.4.1-hotfix).
- Trace bundle: compressed trace file containing request-level events (trace.jsonl.gz).

Required metadata for registry entry

Every experiment must be registered before execution in the experiments table in the Registry service. Minimum fields:

| Field | Example | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| experiment_id | EXP-2025-042 | Assigned by registry UI/CLI |
| owner | eng-serving-runtime/runtime-team | Team and primary oncall |
| hypothesis | "Reduce p95 by < 10% for short-text gen by enabling kernel-waveform v2" | One-line hypothesis |
| artifacts | repo:infra@abcdef, image:runtime:v2025.09@sha256:... | List of artifact snapshots |
| kernel_version | k-2.4.1-hotfix | Kernel and kernel-extensions |
| quant_flags | q4_0, fp16-cache | Quantization flags used |
| traffic_shape | short-gen:60%, long-gen:40% | Traffic mix for synthetic runs |
| seed_traces | s3://exp-bundles/EXP-2025-042/traces/seed-20250912.jsonl.gz | Location of trace bundle |
| benchmark_suite | evbench-v3 | Name of benchmark harness used |
| rollout_plan | canary-5%-24h -> 25%-48h -> 100% | Rollout steps (if planned) |
| sros | runtime-p95:120ms, runtime-p99:450ms, cpu-util:80% | Target SLOs for the experiment |

Registering an experiment

1. Create registry entry via /internal/experiments API or the Registry UI.
2. Attach artifact snapshots and upload seed trace bundle to S3 using cli:infra exp upload-trace --id EXP-XXXX --file traces/seed.jsonl.gz.
3. Add reviewers and link related playbooks (runbooks or chaos scenarios).

Execution protocol (lab run)

1. Reserve a lab-cluster via infra-tag: runtime-lab-XX for the exact kernel and image.
2. Replay seed traces using the Benchmark Harness (evbench-v3):
   - CLI: evbench run --suite evbench-v3 --trace s3://... --concurrency 8 --out s3://exp-results/EXP-2025-042/
3. Collect traces and profiles:
   - runtime-trace-collector --output /tmp/traces --sample 100%
   - perf-kernel-capture --kernel k-2.4.1-hotfix --out /tmp/kernel-profiles
4. Perform profiling: capture GPU counters, kernel dispatch latencies, KV-cache hit breakdowns.
5. Run the standard benchmark matrix: cold-start (10 retries), warm-start (1000 requests), microbursts (10x peak QPS for 10s).

Kernel-scheduler checkpoint and configuration snapshot

Before making scheduler changes, save a checkpoint record that includes:
- Scheduler policy YAML (scheduler-policy.yaml)
- Priority buckets and token rates
- Admission-controller thresholds (tokens per-second)
- Kernel credit accounting config

Store the checkpoint alongside the experiment under s3://runtime-checkpoints/EXP-YYYY-NNN/. Example snippet (scheduler-policy.yaml):

```yaml
priority_buckets:
  - name: interactive
    weight: 100
    token_rate: 200
  - name: batch
    weight: 20
    token_rate: 20
admission:
  max_concurrent: 250
  preemption_enabled: true
```

Observability checklist (required for canary/production experiments)

- p50/p95/p99 latency dashboards for impacted routes
- Kernel dispatch histogram by request_size and model_variant
- KV-cache hit ratio and warmup curve
- Error budget burn rate alert (notify eng-sre)
- Trace correlation ID consistent between runtime-router and kernel-dispatcher

Runbook hooks and anomaly handling

If any of the following occur during a canary:
- latency p95 > target by > 25% for 10m OR
- error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase OR
- kernel crash rate > 0.1%
Then:
1. Pause rollout and scale down canary traffic to 0% (automatic via admission-controller).
2. Trigger experiment incident: tag EXP-XXXX in incident channel #runtime-incidents.
3. Collect last 1h traces and kernel profiles: infra collect-exp-bundle --id EXP-XXXX --window 60m.
4. Engage oncall (owner listed in metadata) and follow the Incident Triage runbook.

Profiling playbook distilled steps

1. Start a controlled replay with sample rate 100% for 1k requests.
2. Capture: compact traces, nvprof counters, kernel-dispatch latency, scheduler token queues.
3. Annotate traces with kernel_version, scheduler-policy hash, and artifact digest.
4. Run causal-attribution script: tools/causal-attrib --before before.tar.gz --after after.tar.gz --out analysis.json

Benchmark mapping and acceptance criteria

- Map each experiment to at least one benchmark in the central suite (evbench-v3, microburst, tail-latency).
- Acceptance: p95 must not regress > 5% for the primary route; p99 regressions require a manual review and explicit approval.

Known-issues capture and linking

When an experiment surfaces a reproducible issue, create an issue entry in the runtime known-issues board and add the following tags: experiment_id, kernel_version, severity (sev1-3). Example known-issue entry fields: [issue_id, experiment_id, summary, repro_steps, traces, owner, mitigation]. Always link the known-issue id back to the experiment registry entry.

Release notes template for experiments that progress to production

- Title: EXP-YYYY-NNN: <short description>
- Summary: one paragraph
- Impacted services: runtime-router, kernel-dispatcher, kv-cache
- SLO deltas observed in canary: p95 before -> after
- Rollout plan: (same as registry)
- Revert instructions: kubectl rollout undo ...; admission-controller rollback command: infra rollback-exp --id EXP-YYYY-NNN
- Contact: owner (email) and oncall rotation

Retention and provenance

- All experiment artifacts (registry entry, traces, kernel checkpoints, profiles) are retained for 540 days in s3://exp-retention/ by default.
- Ownership: the owner field on registry entry is responsible for clean-up and long-term follow-up.

Appendix: quick CLI reference

- Register: infra exp create --id EXP-2025-042 --owner eng-serving-runtime/runtime-team --hypothesis "..."
- Upload trace: infra exp upload-trace --id EXP-2025-042 --file seed.jsonl.gz 
- Start lab run: infra exp run --id EXP-2025-042 --cluster runtime-lab-03 --suite evbench-v3
- Collect bundle: infra exp collect-bundle --id EXP-2025-042 --out s3://exp-results/EXP-2025-042/bundle.tar.gz

Owners and points of contact

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime/runtime-team (Aisha Patel)
- SRE: Diane Chen
- Applied ML liaison: Omar Haddad

If you plan an experiment that touches kernel scheduling, profiling, or rollout mechanics, register it here first and follow this protocol end-to-end. This ensures we preserve reproducibility, reduce blast radius, and make results comparable across runs.
